references.label: NPIS Paracetamol 2012
references.citation: Commission on Human Medicines / National Poisons Information Service. Benefit-risk profile of acetylcysteine in the management of paracetamol overdose: MHRA guidance. 2012 (TOXBASE paracetamol monograph).
references.excerpt: A single treatment nomogram line joining 100 mg/L at 4 hours to 15 mg/L at 15 hours should be used for all patients, irrespective of risk factors, and acetylcysteine should be given to all patients whose plasma paracetamol concentration is on or above this line.

references.label: O'Grady King's Criteria 1989
references.citation: O'Grady JG, Alexander GJM, Hayllar KM, Williams R. Early indicators of prognosis in fulminant hepatic failure. Gastroenterology. 1989;97(2):439-445.
references.excerpt: In paracetamol-induced fulminant hepatic failure, indicators of a poor prognosis warranting consideration for transplantation were arterial pH below 7.30, or the combination of prothrombin time greater than 100 s, serum creatinine greater than 300 micromol/L and grade III or IV encephalopathy.

references.citation: Mahmud N, Fricker Z, Hubbard RA, et al. Risk Prediction Models for Post-Operative Mortality in Patients With Cirrhosis. Hepatology. 2021;73(1):204-218. references.citation: Northup PG, Garcia-Pagan JC, Garcia-Tsao G, et al. Vascular Liver Disorders, Portal Vein Thrombosis, and Procedural Bleeding in Patients With Liver Disease: 2020 AASLD Practice Guidance. Hepatology. 2021;73(1):366-413. Recommends against routine pre-procedural correction of INR or platelets, supports viscoelastic-guided products, and confirms VTE prophylaxis in hospitalised cirrhotics.

references.label: Friedman 2010
references.citation: Friedman LS. Surgery in the patient with liver disease. Trans Am Clin Climatol Assoc. 2010;121:192-204. Classic review establishing that emergency surgery, intra-abdominal/cardiac/hepatic resection, and Child-Pugh class are the dominant determinants of perioperative mortality in cirrhosis.

references.citation: de Franchis R, Bosch J, Garcia-Tsao G, et al. Baveno VII — renewing consensus in portal hypertension. J Hepatol. 2022;76(4):959-974. references.citation: Verbeeck RK / BJA Education review of pharmacokinetics and dosage adjustment in patients with hepatic dysfunction. Eur J Clin Pharmacol. 2008;64(12):1147-1161. cards.question: How is preoperative risk stratified in cirrhosis for non-hepatic surgery?
cards.answer: Combine Child-Pugh class (A/B/C) and MELD score — MELD <10 is low risk, 10–15 intermediate, and >15 high (>20 prohibitive for elective surgery). The VOCAL-Penn score outperforms MELD for surgical mortality prediction.

cards.question: Why should FFP not be used to 'correct' the INR in stable cirrhosis?
cards.answer: Cirrhotic coagulopathy is a rebalanced state — both pro- and anti-coagulant factors are reduced. FFP raises portal pressure (worsening variceal bleeding risk) and adds volume without correcting the underlying defect; thromboelastography (ROTEM/TEG) guides targeted therapy.

cards.question: How is hepatorenal syndrome managed perioperatively?
cards.answer: Splanchnic vasoconstrictor (terlipressin or noradrenaline) plus 20% human albumin (1 g/kg on day 1, then 20–40 g/day). Diuretics, large-volume crystalloid and low-dose dopamine all worsen outcome; definitive treatment is liver transplantation.
